title: San Francisco garter snakes bred in captivity released into wild in conservation milestone
summary: The San Francisco Zoo released 62 captive-bred San Francisco garter snakes into the wild in autumn 2026 at selected sites in San Mateo County, marking the first-ever release of zoo-reared specimens of this endangered species. The non-venomous snakes have been listed as endangered for over 50 years.

title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis CpsA protein inhibits immune clearance via xenophagy suppression
summary: Research published in Science Advances demonstrates that Mycobacterium tuberculosis uses its CpsA protein to disrupt the TBK1-p62 signaling pathway, suppressing xenophagy and allowing the bacterium to evade immune clearance within host cells.
takeaways: CpsA protein classified as LAP (LC3-associated phagocytosis) inhibitor
Protects M. tuberculosis from both NADPH oxidase and xenophagy
Targets TBK1-p62 axis to prevent immune degradation
Allows pathogen persistence within host cells
